items.stem: A valid A/B test of an email should change:

options.text: Several elements at once to save time
options.rationale: Changing several elements makes the cause of any difference unclear.

options.text: One variable at a time between the versions
options.rationale: Correct: isolating one variable lets you attribute the result.

options.text: The audience as well as the content
options.rationale: Changing the audience confounds the test.

options.text: The send time and the subject line together
options.rationale: Two changes at once prevent a clean comparison.

items.explanation: Correct: isolating one variable lets you attribute the result.

items.stem: Permission-based (opt-in) email matters mainly because it:

options.text: Improves engagement and protects deliverability and trust
options.rationale: Correct: willing recipients engage more and keep sender reputation healthy.

options.text: Removes the need to measure results

options.rationale: Honouring unsubscribes is a legal and ethical must.

items.explanation: Correct: willing recipients engage more and keep sender reputation healthy.

items.stem: Which TWO belong in a strong welcome flow for new subscribers? (Select TWO)

options.text: A clear statement of what to expect and how often
options.rationale: Correct: setting expectations reduces later unsubscribes and complaints.

options.text: An early, relevant first value or offer
options.rationale: Correct: delivering early value builds engagement with new subscribers.

options.text: An immediate hard upsell with no context
options.rationale: A cold hard sell at hello tends to increase unsubscribes.

options.text: A long gap before any contact at all
options.rationale: Delaying first contact loses the new subscriber's attention.

items.explanation: Correct: setting expectations reduces later unsubscribes and complaints.; Correct: delivering early value builds engagement with new subscribers.
